Structural Compaction Over Abbreviation: How ASN Tables and Batches Keep Agent Payloads Lean

2026-09-02Token Economy6 min read

These notes were written in September 2026, before the C host was removed, and describe designs as well as shipped behaviour. Where a post says asl-host check or asl-host test, the command today is asl check or asl test; ERR_READ_UNBALANCED is now ERR_UNBALANCED; and the current checker does not reject an unmarked effect (ERR_EFFECT_UNMARKED). Figures are the ones measured on the date each post gives. Current docs

By GenSEAM | September 2026

AgentSlang Notation (ASN) keeps agent payloads and git-tracked memory ledgers compact through structure, not cryptic abbreviations: shared schemas, tabular row layouts and batched tool calls remove repeated keys and wrapper boilerplate across whole collections of records.

When teams first try to shrink agent context, they often reach for character-level abbreviation—shortening function to fn, config to cfg, or message to msg. Under byte-pair tokenizers (cl100k_base, o200k_base), common full words are already single tokens, so abbreviating keywords buys almost nothing while hurting readability and searchability.

In this post we show the BPE measurements behind that design choice (taken with js-tiktoken 1.0.15 on 2026-10-14 for the exact strings shown) and demonstrate how structural compaction in ASN cuts payload size where it actually counts.

1. The Abbreviation Fallacy: Why Shortening Words Fails Under BPE

Byte-pair encoding tokenizers (such as OpenAI's cl100k_base and o200k_base) do not tokenize by character. They assign single token IDs to frequent subwords and whole English words, so common words are already cheap.

The Measurement

Counting single keywords under cl100k_base, first bare and then after a space as they appear inside a form:

KeywordBareIn contextAbbreviationBareIn context
:config22:cfg22
:message12:msg22
:error12:err22
:function12:fn22
:default22:dflt23

Most abbreviations tie in context, and some cost more: :dflt takes 3 tokens where :default takes 2.

The effect across a whole codebase is small. Rewriting every camelCase identifier in the tracked .asl and .asn files (2964 files, 169852 identifiers) to kebab-case and counting both versions gave a saving of 1.90% for camelCase under o200k_base and 1.68% under cl100k_base (measured 2026-09-22, recorded in the project ledger as CamelCaseCorpusSaving and listed in bench/publishedClaims.asn). Naming conventions move token counts by a few percent, not tens of percent.

2. One Spelling per Concept

If shortening keywords does not pay, what should a language choose? AgentSlang's rule is whole words in camelCase and one spelling per concept, and among names that carry the meaning, the measured cheapest wins.

The forms the checker accepts today:

ConceptFormAccepted alias
Functionfn name a: Type -> Type linelambda for anonymous fn
Record typeschema Name with field lines
Variantsenum Name (case field: Type) ...
Matchmatchmt (short alias)
Sequencedobegin
Module exports, imports:x, :i
Primitive typesInt64, Float64, String, Bool

The older defun and df definition heads are rejected by the checker (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TOPLEVEL), and so are :d docstrings (ERR_READ_DOC): documentation lives as rows in each package's doc.asn, not in the source.

(module math/vector :x [dot runTests] :i [])

schema Point
  x: Float64
  y: Float64

fn dot a: Point b: Point -> Float64
  (+ (* a.x b.x) (* a.y b.y))

fn runTests -> Bool
  (do (assert (= (dot {:x 1.0 :y 2.0} {:x 3.0 :y 4.0}) 11.0) "dot product") true)

This module passes asl check and asl test.

3. Rationale Out of Band

Where tokens are wasted in source code is in comments that restate the code:

# Check if the user is authenticated and has permission to access the resource
if user.is_authenticated and user.has_permission(resource):
    allow_access()

The comment repeats what the names already say.

The convention we adopt:

  1. No restating comments: names carry the what.
  2. Docs out of the source: a symbol's contract is one row in the package doc.asn, looked up with asl '(:doc :symbol "path#name")'.
  3. Rationale in the ledger: long design justifications live in the project memory (principles, decisions), where an agent retrieves them only when it needs them, with (:mem :op query ...) or (:query :text "..." :in text).

4. Structural Compaction: Where the Savings Live

If abbreviations do not save tokens, what does? Removing repeated structure.

In JSON tool calls, a large share of the token stream is punctuation (quotes around keys, colons, commas, braces) and key names repeated on every row.

A Command Frame in Four Encodings

  1. JSON (41 tokens under cl100k_base):
{
  "target": "agent-coder",
  "action": "synthesize-fsm",
  "states": ["idle", "active", "error"],
  "timeout_ms": 50
}
  1. TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) (27 tokens):
target: agent-coder
action: synthesize-fsm
states: [idle, active, error]
timeout_ms: 50
  1. Keyed S-expression frame (25 tokens):
(? agent-coder synthesize-fsm :states ["idle" "active" "error"] :timeoutMs 50)
  1. Positional S-expression frame (20 tokens):
(? agent-coder synthesize-fsm ["idle" "active" "error"] 50)

On this frame, moving from JSON to the positional form saves 51.2% under cl100k_base (41 to 20) and 52.4% under o200k_base (42 to 20). The README shows a second frame, a git status command with its arguments, working directory and timeout: 51 tokens as pretty-printed JSON and 18 as a positional frame under cl100k_base, a 64.7% saving. Minified, the same JSON is 30 tokens, so the saving against what is actually sent is 40%, and a positional JSON array of the call is 17 tokens (recounted with tiktoken 0.12.0 on 2026-11-13): the gain is from dropping key names, which any notation can do.

Tabular Data: ASN Against JSON

When agents pass batches of records, JSON repeats every key on every object:

[
  {"id": 101, "sku": "A-44", "qty": 5, "status": "shipped"},
  {"id": 102, "sku": "B-12", "qty": 1, "status": "pending"},
  {"id": 103, "sku": "C-99", "qty": 12, "status": "delivered"}
]

AgentSlang Notation (ASN) states the column names once and streams the rows as positional vectors:

([:id :sku :qty :status]
 [[101 "A-44" 5 "shipped"]
  [102 "B-12" 1 "pending"]
  [103 "C-99" 12 "delivered"]])

These three records take 85 tokens as JSON and 51 as the ASN table under cl100k_base, a 40.0% saving against JSON as written above. Minified, that JSON is 59 tokens, and a minified columnar JSON object with the same header and rows is 49 (recounted with tiktoken 0.12.0 on 2026-11-13), so the row shape, not the notation, carries the saving. The header is paid once, so the share of the stream spent on key names shrinks as rows are added, while JSON pays for every key on every row.

5. Takeaways for Agentic Systems

  1. Stop shortening identifiers: renaming calculateTotal to calcTot saves little or nothing and makes the name harder for a model to recall.
  2. Remove punctuation overhead: quotes, colons and commas around every key are paid on every call; whitespace-separated S-expressions do without them.
  3. Hoist repeated schemas: in multi-record handoffs, send the column names once and the rows as positional vectors.
  4. Keep rationale out of the code: the contract in a doc row, the long justification in the memory ledger.

Structure, not spelling, is where the tokens are. On the samples above, replacing spaced, keyed JSON with positional frames and tables cut token counts by 40.0% to 64.7%; against minified JSON the same frames save 13.6% (table) and 40% (README frame), and JSON in the same positional shape is within two tokens of the S-expression. These are three small samples, not a benchmark.
